archivist_note: Groundwork, with nothing to see on the site. A player noticed that the life totals in a finished game's standings did not match the ones in its analytics chart, and the honest answer turned out to be that the app keeps three different records of what a player finished on and they do not always agree. This release adds an internal check that reconciles all three, game by game and seat by seat, so the question can be asked repeatedly instead of re-derived by hand. It changes nothing you can see and corrects no existing game — deciding which of the three numbers is the true one is a separate conversation, now written down as its own piece of work.

resolved: The Donate link at the bottom of the desktop sidebar could disappear, taking the last nav row with it, when the browser window was short. It now stays pinned and fully visible at the bottom of the sidebar at any window height, with the nav groups above it scrolling on their own.
archivist_note: Reported as the Donate button going wonky on a short window, and it turned out to be two faults stacked. The sidebar's nav was told to be as tall as the whole sidebar, forgetting that the Collapse button and a gap already sit in that same space — so it always ran about fifty pixels long. And an old style rule left over from a navigation bar we retired years ago was quietly telling that column it was allowed to wrap, which sent the overflow sideways out past the edge of the sidebar rather than down. Both are fixed, and the layout was measured in a real browser at five window heights across all three sidebar states rather than eyeballed.

refined: On a finished game's summary, each bar in the Pace strip is now filled with that player's color from the life chart, and hovering a bar names the player and the round it was played in — so you can see at a glance whose turns were the long ones. This works for games you play from now on and for every game already recorded.
archivist_note: The Pace strip knew how long each turn took but not whose turn it was — turn events were never recorded against a seat. Rather than leave older games grey, the summary now reconstructs the seating rotation from the game's own event history, skipping players as they were eliminated and bringing them back if they were revived. A caution worth stating plainly: the strip reflects what the app was told during the game. If a turn was tapped twice by mistake, that mistake is in the picture too.

refined: In companion mode, only the player whose turn it is can end the turn from their phone. The End turn button now stays disabled and shows whose turn it actually is until your turn comes around. The shared tablet running the table view keeps full control and can still advance the turn for anyone, in any order — including for a guest seat that isn't linked to an account.
archivist_note: Any seated player could advance the turn from their own phone, which made an accidental tap someone else's problem. The turn now belongs to the person taking it. We kept one deliberate escape hatch: the table view can always move the turn, so if the tracker ever falls out of step with the physical table, the tablet fixes it rather than the game getting stuck.

resolved: The Current price column on your Wishlist was blank for cards you don't own — which is most of a wishlist. It now shows the cheapest current price from the daily card-price cache, so any-printing wishlist entries display a price whether or not you own a copy.
archivist_note: The app keeps a full local copy of card prices, refreshed daily — and one of the main reasons it exists is exactly this: to price a card you're hunting but don't own yet. The Wishlist just wasn't consulting it for those rows. Owned cards were never affected; their prices come from the more precise source and still do.

added: Colour and card-type filters everywhere the wishlist and trades show cards: your own wishlist, a shared wishlist link, the members' wishlists on a playgroup page, and both sides of the trade proposal form. Pick a colour, a type, or both, and the list narrows as you choose — no page reload, and it stacks with the name box and everything else already on screen.
archivist_note: "Green" here means cards that are green, which is a different question from the one the Collection's colour pips answer — those show what you could cast in a deck of those colours, so they include colourless cards. Both are right for their own surface, and they are kept deliberately distinct. Colourless and Multicolour are their own choices rather than something you have to infer.

added: Sorting and filtering on the Wishlist. Sort by name, current price, target price, date added, or how many copies you own; narrow the list to cards whose target price has been met, cards you don't own yet, or ones you already do; and filter by name as you type.
resolved: Card images on a completed trade were rendering as blank frames. The record kept for a finished trade was missing the one identifier the image server needs, so every card came up empty. Fixed — and the card view now falls back to a clean placeholder rather than a broken frame if an image can't be built.
archivist_note: Both items came from SaintWacko on the same afternoon. The image bug is the second of its kind in a week — the same field missing from a different copy of the same idea — so alongside the fix we made the card view refuse to draw an image it can't actually build. A blank frame is worse than no frame: it looks like the card is missing rather than the picture.

added: Your side of the trade form now shows where each card lives — "Deck · Atraxa", "Binder · Mythics", "Drawer 2" — with deck cards called out, plus a Location sort so they group together. Offering a card that's currently in a deck means taking that deck apart, and now you can see that before you offer it rather than after.
archivist_note: Only your own cards show a location. The other player's side shows the card and nothing else — where they keep their collection is theirs, and the trade form has never been able to see it.

added: A "Picked only" checkbox on the trade form's card pickers. Tick it and the list collapses to just the cards you've selected — most useful when a trade is started from someone's wishlist, which fills your side in automatically and previously left you scrolling your whole collection to weed out the ones you'd rather keep.
archivist_note: The filter re-applies when you tick it, not continuously — so removing a card leaves the row where it is instead of making it disappear under your cursor. Hiding a card never un-picks it; it is only a view.

added: Prices on the trade proposal form. Every card in both pickers now shows what it's worth, and a running total at the bottom of the page tracks both sides as you pick — "You give $41.00 · You get $38.50" — with a note when the two sides are within a dollar of each other. Proxies count as nothing, and a card we have no price for says so rather than showing $0.00.
archivist_note: Proposed trades already showed a per-side total once they were sent; what was missing was seeing the numbers while you build one, which is when they can still change your mind. The totals bar sticks to the bottom of the window so it stays with you through a few hundred cards. It is guidance, not a rule — nothing stops you sending a lopsided offer, and there are plenty of good reasons to.

resolved: The new sort control on the trade form could look broken after a page reload: the browser puts your last choice back in the dropdown, but the list stayed in its original order. The sort is now applied as the page loads, so what the dropdown says is always what you see.

added: The trade form's card pickers can now be sorted — by name, mana value, set, rarity, price, or how many are available — on both sides of the deal. Sorting is instant and never disturbs what you've already picked.
A "Card images" toggle on the same pickers, so you can see what each card actually does instead of reading a list of names.
resolved: Card images on shared Showcases were rendering broken. They now load properly.
archivist_note: A small quality-of-life pass on the trade construction page, asked for by SaintWacko — picking cards out of a few hundred names sorted only by when they were added is a chore, and names alone don't tell you what a card does. Sorting here is done in the browser rather than by reloading the page, which is a departure from every other sorted list in the app: the picks you've made on this page live only in the page itself until you send the proposal, so a reload would quietly throw them away. The sort values still come from the same one place the rest of the app sorts by. Looking into it turned up an unrelated bug — the read-only card view used on shared Showcases had been leaving out the one field the image server needs, so those images had been silently broken. Fixed in the same pass.

added: A "Propose a trade" button on a shared wishlist. Open someone's wishlist, and if you already own cards they're after, the trade form opens with those cards filled in on your side — you just pick what you'd like back from their Showcase. Only copies that are actually free to trade get filled in; anything sitting in a deck stays put unless you add it yourself.

A [pending] tag on wishlist entries a playgroup member has already offered in a trade, so nobody spends an evening tracking down a card someone else is already bringing. It shows that a card is covered — never who is covering it, and never on a public wishlist link.
refined: On the trade form, cards on your side of the deal can now be un-picked as easily as picked.
archivist_note: The trade tie-in that both wishlist releases deferred, requested by Alex. Two decisions shaped it. The first: a wishlist-seeded proposal is one-sided by nature, and trades here have always required something on both sides. We kept that rule rather than inventing a gift path — the button seeds your half and leaves the asking to you. The second: the [pending] tag deliberately widens what a third party can see, so we drew the line at aggregate. Covered, not covered-by-whom, and never on a link anyone can open. Both parts reuse machinery already in place — the ownership matching came free from the wishlist release before it, and the badge costs one query per page. No schema change.

resolved: Closed a way a deck's card list could be corrupted: a card already committed to one deck could be pulled into another, quietly emptying it out of the first. Pulling a card into a deck now only ever takes a loose copy from your collection, never one that's already living in another deck.
archivist_note: v4.11.34 = two hygiene fixes off the reconciled Known-Problems list. (1) pull_card_to_deck now rejects a source InventoryRow whose location type is deck/considering — the #27 residual where POST /decks/pull was the one remaining path that could relocate a card out from under a sibling (or any) deck, since it fetched the row by id+user with no loose-source guard. Mirrors the type NOT IN (deck, considering) rule _get_loose_source_rows already enforces for switch-printing / reconciliation. (2) Deleted the ~190-line unreachable auth-CSRF cluster in dependencies.py (require_csrf_or_reissue / csrf_state / _classify_session_cookie / _classify_cross_site / _log_no_session + _SESSION_MAX_AGE) — superseded by require_preauth_csrf since #63, zero callers, ruff-clean so it had hidden for months. A third listed item — the Switch Printing full-width button — was found already resolved (the modal CSS was reworked; no auto-fit/stretch remains), so the stale Known-Problem entry was corrected rather than 'fixed'. Not user-facing beyond (1); no schema. Tests: pull-guard cases in test_pull_proxy_lifecycle.py; suite 1078 green.

added: Your collection CSV/JSON export now includes each deck card's format. Cards that live in a deck carry a "Deck Format" column (Commander, Modern, and so on); cards on a shelf or in a binder leave it blank.
refined: Importing more copies of a card you already have no longer overwrites the note on the existing row. If both the existing row and the incoming one have notes, your original note is kept rather than replaced.
When an import spreads cards across several locations, the results page now lists them per place — "12 cards at Binder · 3 cards at Deck: Atraxa" — instead of a bare "2 locations".

resolved: The goldfish playtester's board returns to its earlier layout. A recent change reorganized the battlefield into two zones with a docked mana pool and a commander-cast counter — but that was an accidental second take on a layout adjustment already shipped, and it over-corrected. This restores the intended single version: the card preview shares the right rail with the command zone, the graveyard sits on the left rail beside the library and exile, the battlefield is one open zone, and the mana pool returns to its floating widget.
archivist_note: v4.11.32 reverts commit 8f8fee1 (v4.11.29). v4.11.29 was an accidental second application of the SaintWacko layout-mockup task already shipped in v4.11.26; the second pass over-corrected the layout. This revert restores the intended single application (the v4.11.26 layout). v4.11.30 (#149) and v4.11.31 (#148) landed after v4.11.29 and are preserved — the revert touched only the three goldfish files (goldfish.js, style.css, goldfish.html); the README and chronicle conflicts were resolved by keeping all history and appending this entry rather than deleting the v4.11.29 one.

added: Decks now have a "Considering" section — a holding area for cards you're weighing while you brew, kept separate from the deck itself. Stage cards you own, or (on a brew) unowned placeholders, see at a glance which you already have, and promote a card into the deck or set it aside with one click. Considering cards never count toward your deck's size, stats, legality, exports, the playtester, or its public share page until you promote them — so you can pile up ideas without skewing anything. Requested by SaintWacko.

resolved: Fixed the deck Grid/List view toggle getting stuck. If you had filtered or sorted a deck's card list, the page's web address quietly picked up your current view — and after that the Grid/List button stopped switching, until you reopened the deck from your deck list. View mode is now purely a saved preference, so the toggle always takes effect no matter what's in the URL. Reported by SaintWacko.

added: The goldfish playtester got a cleaner board. The battlefield is now two open zones — Battlefield up top for your permanents and a dedicated Lands zone below it — instead of the five auto-sorted boxes, so the table reads at a glance. The mana pool is now docked into the right rail (under Command) as a tidy stack of W/U/B/R/G/C rows rather than a floating widget, and the Command area gained a Cast counter with an automatic commander-tax readout (tax = 2 × times cast). Layout from a community mockup by SaintWacko.

When you open a wishlist someone shared with you — either their public link or a playgroup member's list — Cartarch now marks the cards you already own, shows WHERE your copies are (e.g. "2× Binder · Mythics · 1× Deck · Atraxa"), and tallies "you own 8 of 20" at the top. It's the fast answer to "do I have anything off their list I could trade or gift, and where is it?" without cross-checking by hand. Proxies don't count as owned. Anyone viewing without an account sees the plain names-only page, unchanged; the ownership marks are your own numbers and appear only when you're signed in. Follow-up to the wishlist sharing, requested by Alex.
archivist_note: A shared wishlist answers "what do you want"; the natural next question is "what of it do I already have." We could answer it the same way the deck checker does — the ownership lookup was already written and battle-tested — so this was a matter of pointing an existing tool at a new page rather than inventing anything. The one careful line: the owner's page stays exactly as private as it was, because the marks we add are the viewer's own collection, never a peek into someone else's.

added: You can share your wishlist now — two ways. From the Wishlist page you can create a public link that anyone can open (no account needed), or turn on visibility for any playgroup you're in, so your fellow members see it right on the playgroup page. Either way, viewers see only the card names: your notes, target prices, and what you already own stay private. Revoke the public link or stop sharing with a playgroup any time. Requested by Alex.
archivist_note: The interesting constraint on a shared wishlist is what it must NOT reveal. A wishlist doubles as a budget (the target prices) and a quiet map of what you already have (the ownership counts) — none of which is anyone else's business just because you want to tell them which cards you're after. So the shared view is built from a short list of allowed fields, and on the fully-public link even your name is only shown if you set a display name, never the email you sign in with.

refined: The goldfish playtester's board reclaims its wasted whitespace. The card preview, which used to sit in its own column on the right, now shares the right rail with the command zone, and the graveyard moved over to the left rail beside the library and exile. With both sides pinned to narrow rails, the battlefield in the middle gets roughly a card and a half wider before you need to scroll. Narrow screens are unchanged. Layout from a mockup by SaintWacko.

added: You can add cards from a brew's buy-list straight to your wishlist. Each 'To buy' and 'Partially owned' section now has a '+ wishlist all' button, and every card in those sections has its own '+ wishlist' — one tap and it's tracked. Cards already on your wishlist are simply skipped (the wishlist tracks a card once, so nothing gets duplicated), and a small banner tells you how many were added. Requested by SaintWacko.
refined: Internal cleanup: removed a batch of dead code that guarded a database constraint retired in the v4 Postgres move (the old cross-user deck-name conflict handling). No visible change.

added: The goldfish playtester now has a dice roller and a coin flip. A small '🎲' dropdown in the controls offers d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20 and a coin; click one and the result shows right on the trigger, so the last roll stays visible without reopening the menu. It closes the same way every other popover does — click away or press Escape. Requested by SaintWacko.

refined: The public deck share page now shows the deck's color identity as mana symbols in its header (they were being computed but not drawn). A small polish on the share links added moments earlier.

added: Share a deck with anyone — no account required. On a deck's page, open 'Share' and create a public link; anyone you send it to sees a clean, read-only copy of the decklist (grouped by card type, with the commander and color identity up top). Prices, what you own vs. proxy, tags, and your private notes are all hidden — only the deck's blurb comes along. The link is a long unguessable code, so a deck stays private until you make one, and 'Revoke' turns it off instantly (or 'Regenerate' rolls a fresh link and retires the old one). Requested by SaintWacko.
archivist_note: The quiet discipline here is what the shared page does NOT contain. A collection manager knows a lot about your cards you'd never want a stranger to see — what each is worth, which ones you're only proxying, your working notes — so the public view is built from a short allow-list of fields rather than by hiding things one at a time. What's on the page is exactly what was chosen to be there, and nothing arrives by accident.

resolved: A quick correction to the ramp fix in the previous release. In tightening up ramp detection we briefly also counted a card's 'search for a basic land' clause even when that land goes to an opponent — so a few removal spells (Path to Exile, Assassin's Trophy) and land-destruction cards read as ramp for a moment. That's undone: only mana granted to permanents you control counts. Group ramp where everyone fetches a land (Collective Voyage) is a separate, harder call and stays on the list rather than being guessed at.

Cards that give your other permanents a mana ability now count as ramp. Cryptolith Rite ('Creatures you control have "tap: Add one mana of any color"') and Bootleggers' Stash are textbook ramp, but the tagger skipped the quoted granted ability wholesale — a rule that correctly ignores a token's own mana ability (Sifter of Skulls) and a mana ability handed to an opponent's creature by a removal aura (Utopia Vow). Now the phrase 'you control' is the tell: a mana ability granted to permanents you control counts, while token abilities and opponent-facing auras still don't. Deck-health ramp counts update immediately; the tag chips on cards you already own are being brought in line in a follow-up pass. Reported by SaintWacko, who had been hand-tagging these one at a time.
archivist_note: A quiet false negative is harder to notice than a false positive — nothing looks wrong, a real ramp card just isn't counted — and the tell was that people had started fixing it by hand, one card at a time, without saying anything. The fix hangs on two words: 'you control' is the difference between a mana ability you get to use and one that belongs to a token or an opponent's creature. Reading who the mana is actually for is the whole game.

resolved: Cards you don't own in a brew deck no longer leak into your collection. When you add an unowned card to a brew, it's created as a proxy placeholder — but that placeholder used to show up in your collection like something you owned, and if the card left the deck it turned into a real owned copy you never had. Now a brew placeholder stays put in its deck: it's kept out of your collection list, counts, exports, and pill totals; it can't be moved out, showcased, or offered in a trade; and if you delete it from the deck it's simply discarded rather than fabricated into an owned card. Real cards and physical proxies you actually own are completely unaffected. Reported by SaintWacko.
archivist_note: The tell was subtle — a brew is meant to be a wish-list you can playtest, so the cards in it that you don't own shouldn't quietly pad your real collection. They had been ordinary inventory rows all along, which is why they wandered where they didn't belong. Rather than re-plumb how deck cards are stored, we drew one line — a proxy sitting in a brew deck is a placeholder, not a possession — and taught every door it might slip through to recognize it.

resolved: The card actions menu works again in a deck's list view. Opening the "⋮" menu on a card in list mode had started landing the menu in the wrong place — floating over other cards instead of under the button you clicked — so it looked like nothing happened and the Switch printing option seemed to vanish. It now opens neatly beneath its card, with every action present, and no longer shoves the surrounding list around when it appears. Reported by SaintWacko.
archivist_note: A tidy one. The list view packs cards into newspaper-style columns to fit more on screen, and that column layout quietly disagreed with how the actions menu figured out where to appear — the two features were each fine alone and only misbehaved together. We pinned the menu to float above the page rather than live inside the columns, and it snaps back to where your finger expects it.

resolved: Cards that make themselves cheaper are no longer mistaken for ramp. "This spell costs {7} less to cast" is a discount on one spell, not acceleration — but the tagger counted it as ramp all the same, so counterspells and board wipes were filed as ramp and quietly padded a deck's ramp count. 326 cards across the card pool were affected. Reported by SaintWacko, whose Not of This World — a counterspell — was being called expensive ramp. Tags already saved against your cards were written by the old reading and are being corrected in a follow-up pass, so a card you have tagged may take a little longer to catch up.

Counterspells that name what they counter are recognized again. "Counter target creature spell", "Counter target noncreature spell", "Counter target activated or triggered ability" — the tagger expected the word it was looking for to come immediately after "target", so every counterspell with a qualifier in between matched nothing and came back with no role at all. 27 cards in the collection get their role back.
archivist_note: Two unrelated repairs, filed apart and shipped together because they were found on the same afternoon. The first was reported: a player looked at a counterspell labelled expensive ramp and said, plainly, that it was not ramp. He was right, and the fault ran wider than his card — anything that discounted itself was being read as though it accelerated something. The second was never reported by anyone, because its symptom was an absence: a counterspell with a qualifier in its text simply came back with no role at all, and a card that says nothing about itself attracts no complaints. It was found only because the first bug sent someone reading the same few lines. They share a neighbourhood in the code and nothing else, and we have left them as two.

resolved: Buying a card your brew was proxying now retires the proxy, even when the copy you bought is a different printing or finish than the placeholder. Before, the deck kept both — two copies of a card in a singleton deck — and the buy-list went on asking you to buy something already sitting in the deck.
archivist_note: A proxy in a brew is a note that reads "I don't own this yet." The previous fix retired that note only when the card you bought matched the placeholder exactly — same printing, same finish — which is not how buying cards works. You find a copy, and it is the copy that was there. So the note stayed pinned next to the real card it was standing in for, the deck quietly held two of a card it is only allowed one of, and the shopping list kept recommending a purchase already made. The rule now matches the intent it always had: the note is about the card, not the particular version of it, and any copy retires it. Which printing you own still matters everywhere it should — the deck holds the one you actually bought, and a foil stays a foil.

added: Deck list view now reaches every card action the grid view offers. Each row carries a menu with tags, commander, switch printing, remove from deck, and move to location — the same set, from the same source, so the two views can no longer disagree about what you can do to a card.
resolved: The commander no longer escapes its panel and joins the deck list. Sorting, searching, or regrouping a deck used to shuffle it in among the other cards; it now stays where it belongs no matter how the list is rearranged.
Adding a card while reading a deck in list view no longer snaps you back to grid view.
archivist_note: Three complaints, one habit. The deck page can redraw its card list without reloading the page, and each of the several paths that trigger that redraw had been taught, separately, how to assemble the list. Every one of them forgot something different — two forgot that the commander belongs in its own panel, a third forgot which view you were reading in. None of this was visible until you rearranged a list and watched your commander wander into it. The repair was to stop teaching each path its own version of the answer and let them all ask the same one; the fix is smaller than the bugs it closes, which is usually the sign that the cause was found rather than the symptom.

refined: The card-intelligence Phase 0 validation is now evidence-first. Before any conclusions, the report reconciles deployment state (production vs. `main` vs. latest release, with commit SHA, image digest, and migration head), maps every requirement to concrete code, test, or schema evidence under a defined evidence hierarchy, and profiles identity fields for real data-quality risks rather than row counts. The predetermined `oracle_id` first PR is replaced by a ranked first-increment recommendation, and closure of #122 stays contingent on human review.
archivist_note: The original plan had the right intent — inspect the system and decide on evidence — but it prematurely concluded on architecture, naming a mandatory first PR and assuming a schema before the repository had been read. That is how a validation report quietly becomes an implementation order aimed at a deployment state nobody confirmed. The revisions turn every conclusion back into a hypothesis and pin it to a reconciled baseline, so the report describes the system as it actually is and leaves the first build step to be chosen, not assumed.

resolved: Build-gate fix for the v4.11.12 timezone flip — no user-facing change.
archivist_note: v4.11.13 = CI-gate hotfix for v4.11.12 (#130). Enabling ruff DTZ in v4.11.12 was verified against app/ tests/ alembic/ but CI runs `ruff check .` over the WHOLE repo and flagged a naive datetime literal in scripts/validate_cutover.py:190 (a cutover-probe INSERT sentinel), failing the lint gate — so v4.11.12 built NO image and never deployed (prod stayed v4.11.11). Fix: updated_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1) -> datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC). No app-code, model, or migration change; the whole #130 flip rides in v4.11.12's records. Lesson: the DTZ enablement should have been validated with `ruff check .` (CI's scope), not a path subset.

resolved: Timestamps across the app are now timezone-aware UTC end to end (Postgres timestamptz), removing the naive/aware ambiguity so dates and times compute and display correctly everywhere.
archivist_note: v4.11.12 = #130 (the deferred v3.36.13 single-flip-point). utc_now() flipped naive->aware (datetime.now(UTC)); a new UTCDateTime TypeDecorator (impl timestamptz) re-attaches UTC on read so SQLite tests read aware exactly like prod psycopg does — kills the naive-vs-aware TypeError class at the type boundary rather than at every call site. Migration e1f2a3b4c5d6 converts 49 naive columns to timestamptz via USING col AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' (enumerated from information_schema at runtime, idempotent); 1 pre-existing tz column skipped (deck_card_shares.created_at, #27). UTC-convention proven against prod 2026-07-15: deck_bracket_estimates.generated_at read 13:04 UTC at a ~09:45 Central wall-clock moment — a local-Central reading would be in the future (impossible), so naive stored values ARE UTC and the conversion needs no offset correction. 9-site straggler sweep: 8 datetime.now(UTC) bypasses routed through timeutil + 1 naive strptime made aware, plus audit_service datetime.min -> aware, editorial filter strptime -> date.fromisoformat, gc_sync date.today -> utc_now().date(). ruff DTZ (flake8-datetimez) enabled to lock the door — production DTZ-clean; tests keep only DTZ001 (naive fixtures bind-normalize) while every other DTZ rule stays active. Deploy note (honest): PreSync applies the migration BEFORE the pod swap, so the outgoing naive-code pod briefly serves aware timestamptz reads — its display filter and aware-vs-aware math tolerate that, but auth-adjacent naive-vs-aware comparisons (login throttle, reset expiry, last-active) can TypeError for the sub-two-minute window (~9 users, self-healing at swap); the new code never sees naive columns. Suite 970 green. Prod behavior unchanged (psycopg already returned aware for timestamptz).

resolved: Acquiring a card your brew was holding as a proxy now correctly marks it owned: pulling or importing the real copy into the deck consumes the proxy instead of silently stacking onto it, so the buy-list no longer lists cards you already have.
archivist_note: v4.11.11 = #134 (proxy lifecycle). pull_card_to_deck's merge key was is_proxy-blind, so a real copy pulled into a brew merged onto the proxy row (is_proxy stayed True; build_brew_buylist kept reading owned=0/missing). Fix: proxy-aware merge key (real->real, proxy->proxy; created deck rows carry the source's is_proxy) PLUS consume-the-proxy semantics — decrement the deck's proxy of the same (card_id, finish) by the pulled quantity and delete at zero (delete_shares_for_inventory_row + clean_inventory_row_references), matching materialize_brew's intent; a surviving proxy beside the new real row would be two copies of one card in a singleton deck. Second is_proxy-blind site closed: _commit_deck_import_with_reconciliation's auto-merge keyed on (card_id, finish) -> now (card_id, finish, is_proxy). The Add-tab owned-copy move (#119) already routes through pull_card_to_deck, so it's covered by the same fix. Tests: tests/test_pull_proxy_lifecycle.py (consume / multi-proxy shrink / excess / finish-mismatch no-cross-consume / real-row merge regression) + an import-path integration case in tests/test_import_brew_proxy.py. archivist_note: vX.Y.Z = #95, Phase 3. NOTE: `state.turn` is the ROUND counter (bumps only when the rotation wraps past the first seat), so the life x-axis is rounds. Test drives the REAL service chain (start_live_game -> apply_live_action life/cmd/turn -> end_game) so payloads can't drift from the writer, asserting life finals (coupled cmd+life), the elimination order/cause/remaining, the lethal cmd cell, and pace; plus the no-events None case. archivist_note: v4.6.4 = hotfix for Momir activation being dead in prod since v4.6.0. Root cause: app/jobs/oracle_ingest.py never set a User-Agent, so Scryfall rejected every request with HTTP 400 (generic_user_agent) and the ingest failed on the first call — oracle_catalog stayed empty, valid_momir_mvs() returned {} and the MV picker greyed out entirely. Masked because tests mock the fetch and Phase 0 recon used curl (which sends its own UA). Fix: descriptive User-Agent + Accept on both requests.get calls (index + bulk download), pinned by a monkeypatched test that fails on a default UA. Also dropped the per-process valid_momir_mvs memo: it couldn't be invalidated across processes (a job-pod ingest can't bust a web-pod cache), so a freshly-populated catalog stayed invisible until a manual rollout restart. Now queried live (DISTINCT over the indexed is_momir_legal column, sub-ms, only on a Momir render); removed invalidate_valid_mvs and callers. Prod hot-fixed out of band before this shipped: ran the corrected ingest (19,752 rows, 17.5k legal) against cartarch-prod Postgres + rolled the web pod to clear the stale memo. Suite 864 green.

added: The Momir simulator now has a full table + phone interface. Each player shows their library, hand, and lands (with untapped mana) and a Play Land button; the mana-value picker greys out costs you can't pay or that have no creatures.
Creatures show effective power/toughness with counters, marked damage, keyword badges, and tapped / summoning-sick indicators, with the full rules text a tap away.

Combat is guided end to end: tap a creature to attack a player, and the defender picks any number of blockers (the app enforces flying, menace, and untapped rules). Resolve abilities right on a creature — damage, +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters, tap, sacrifice, revive.
resolved: Momir Sim phase 5 (#113): tablet + phone UI over the phase 1-4 engine. All Momir-only; Commander games show none of it.
archivist_note: v4.6.3 = Momir Sim phase 5 (#113), the UI over the phases 1-4 engine. Tablet game_detail.html + phone game_companion.html, both SSE-driven full-state render, Momir-only. Per-seat resource bar (library/hand/lands/untapped/landPlayed): tablet has tap-to-correct steppers via momir_adjust (table-token), phone is read-only (adjust is table-only) + momir_play_land. MV picker greys MVs with no legal creature (valid_momir_mvs injected into the render context in routes/games.py, no separate endpoint) and unaffordable MVs (> untapped); Activate/go gated on empty hand / spent quota / off-turn.
